name: Rough Cut To Second Pass Workflow
use_when: A talking-head, tutorial, commentary, or YouTube video needs to move from raw footage to a polished edit.
The editor is tempted to add effects before the story and pacing are working.
A long timeline needs a repeatable pass structure for cutting, B-roll, audio, and export.
A DaVinci Resolve short should move from simple postable edit to Fusion polish to reusable presets.
A Premiere plus After Effects Reel needs a stable prepared cut before animation.
A scripted viral-style YouTube video needs voiceover, music, assets, animations, SFX, and color organized into repeatable passes.
A short-form story needs original, shorter, and balanced timeline versions compared before final polish.
A Resolve project needs a full page-based pass order from Media to Deliver.
avoid_when: The user asks for a single tiny trim or technical conversion.
The source footage is already locked and only finishing work is needed.
The project is experimental and the user explicitly wants discovery through visual treatment first.

timeline_pattern.pattern: project_setup -> import -> rough_cut -> remove_dead_time -> add_motivated_visuals -> second_pass_polish -> color_pass -> audio_pass -> export_qc
timeline_pattern.rough_cut_rule: The first pass should make the edit watchable and understandable before effects are added.
timeline_pattern.second_pass_rule: The second pass should tighten, hide rough cuts, add proof visuals, improve focus, and repair audio.
timeline_pattern.save_rule: Save before risky timeline operations and keep duplicate sequences for major versions.
timeline_pattern.phase_rule: For Resolve shorts, phase one is clean vertical A-roll/B-roll/captions, phase two is Fusion polish, and phase three is Power Bin/preset efficiency.
timeline_pattern.ae_roundtrip_rule: For Premiere plus After Effects reels, organize assets, sync/prep footage, trim and correct the prepared cut, ideate segments, animate in AE, render back to Premiere, then finish SFX/music/captions/export.
timeline_pattern.script_asset_rule: For scripted YouTube edits, tag the script into visual asset categories and gather media before the heavy timeline pass.
timeline_pattern.review_rule: After the first rough assembly, rewatch cold, add missing support, remove boring lines, and rewrite only when it improves the main goal.
timeline_pattern.versioning_rule: Use named duplicate or stacked timelines to compare original, shorter, and balanced pacing before committing polish.
timeline_pattern.resolve_full_rule: For full Resolve projects, organize Media first, assemble in Edit/Cut, then move through Fusion, Color, Fairlight, and Deliver after story timing is stable.

motion.rule: Delay decorative motion until the cut order, spoken logic, and visual motivation are clear.

sound.rule: Do a dedicated audio pass after the rough cut so dialogue, music, and SFX can be balanced in context. If music is added early for vibe, re-check the final full mix after SFX.

captions.rule: Add or refine captions after the spoken sequence is locked enough that caption timing will not be churned.

color.rule: Correct obvious mismatches during polish, but save full look work until picture timing is stable.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent the rough cut as an EDL or concat list, then render short review exports before adding overlay, caption, and audio filters.
implementation.remotion: Create named sequences for rough_cut, visual_support, polish, audio_mix, and export_qc so each pass is inspectable.
implementation.blender: Only build animated inserts once the surrounding timeline duration and narration beat are stable.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create a rough duplicate, trim dead time, then add overlays, captions, music, and SFX in later passes.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use duplicate sequences, bins, labels, markers, and manual saves; keep rough, polish, prepared, animation, finish, and export versions separate. For scripted viral videos, import VO, trim by script, optionally add licensed/platform-safe music for vibe, layer assets from script tags, then do animation, SFX, color, and export passes. In Resolve, use Media organization, Edit/Cut assembly, Fusion polish, Color matching/look, Fairlight mix, and Deliver settings in that order.

common_mistakes: Polishing a section before knowing whether it belongs.
Opening Fusion before the simple short is clean, vertical, captioned, and motivated.
Adding effects to hide a weak idea or unclear spoken logic.
Skipping the audio pass because the timeline looks visually finished.
Exporting from a messy working sequence without checking version, in/out range, and settings.
Choosing the shortest version even when it removes the human connection or proof that made the story work.
Starting After Effects work before the prepared cut and segment plan are stable.
Opening the timeline without a script asset map and hunting for every visual mid-edit.
Adding music early and never rechecking whether it still fits after the edit changes.
Doing Color, Fairlight, or Deliver work before the selected story timeline is clear.
qc: Can the rough cut be understood without decorative effects?
Are all B-roll, overlays, and captions attached to a spoken or story purpose?
Was an audio pass completed after major trims?
Is the export taken from the intended locked sequence and range?
For Resolve shorts, did the edit pass through simple cut, Fusion polish, and preset/QC review in that order?
For Premiere plus After Effects reels, was a prepared render reviewed before animation began?
Does each scripted beat have an asset/visual decision before heavy timeline work?
Was the rough cut rewatched for add, remove, and rewrite decisions before final polish?
Were major duration versions compared and clearly named before the final version was polished?
For Resolve projects, did Media, Edit/Cut, Fusion, Color, Fairlight, and Deliver each receive the appropriate pass?
